content: Healthcare providers are advised to develop and implement standardized protocols for routine psychosocial screening. These screenings are essential to identify psychological and social factors that may interfere with effective diabetes management. Specific issues to assess include diabetes-related distress, clinical depression, anxiety disorders, and fear of hypoglycemia. Such screenings should be conducted on a regular basis and should also evaluate external stressors, such as recent changes in the patient’s health status or shifts in family support systems.
